title: Reliability of CKA as a Similarity Measure in Deep Learning (Davari, Horoi, Natik, Lajoie, Wolf, Belilovsky; arXiv 2210.16156v2, Nov 2022)

setup.data: Synthetic: 10K points uniform in a 1K-dimensional unit cube at the origin plus 10K points in a cube centred at (1.1, 0, ..., 0), linearly separable on dimension 1. CIFAR10 (10k training images for the translation test; test set for reported results). Patch Camelyon (CKA maps under distribution shift). CIFAR-10C (OOD accuracy after CKA manipulation).
setup.models: Vision only, no language models: a 9-layer CNN (8 conv + 1 FC, from Kornblith et al. 2019 Sec 6.1), trained as generalised, memorised (random labels), or left randomly initialised; ResNet-34 at widths x1, x2, x4, x5; VGG-style nets at widths x1, x2, x4, x8, x10; a small ViT (8 blocks, 12 heads, hidden size 256).
setup.positions_layers: Layer-by-layer CKA maps over all layers; layers 1-2 for the generalised/memorised/random comparison; the last hidden layer before the output for the SVM-preserving translation test and the PCA of manipulated representations.
setup.baselines: Original (unmanipulated) CKA maps and accuracies (e.g. CNN 85.9%, ResNet-34 x1 93.7%, VGG x1 85.9%, ViT 88.7%); published CKA conclusions of Kornblith et al. (2019) and Nguyen et al. (2021, 2022).
setup.controls: Distillation loss (or cross-entropy variant) to keep outputs while the CKA map is optimised, with an accuracy tolerance that scales lambda; results reported on the test set; OOD accuracy on CIFAR-10C; linear-probe accuracy as a usefulness check next to CKA; same vs different seeds; 5 seeds (Fig 2); 10 random instantiations (Fig 9); several RBF bandwidths (0.2, 0.4, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0 x median distance); minibatch CKA with the unbiased HSIC estimator.

key_results.claim: Headline: CKA can be manipulated while the model's function barely changes.
key_results.quote: the CKA value can be easily manipulated without substantial changes to the functional behaviour of the models, and call for caution when leveraging activation alignment metrics.

key_results.claim: Theorem 1: translating a subset of representations can drive linear CKA down; the limit is Gamma(rho) x ||E_S[x]||^2 / E||x||^2 x sqrt(participation ratio), with Gamma(rho) = rho/(1-rho).
key_results.quote: any set of internal neural representations X (e.g., from hidden layers of a network) can be manipulated with simple transformations (translations of a subset

key_results.claim: Such a translation can be functionally inert: the next layer ignores it if its weights are orthogonal to the shift direction.
key_results.quote: it is also easy to eliminate or ignore in a single layer transformation, as long as the weight vectors associated with the neurons in the subsequent layer

key_results.claim: Corollary 3: a single far-moved outlier can make two nearly identical sets look dissimilar.
key_results.quote: This will drastically lower the CKA value between the two considered representations despite their obvious similarity.

key_results.claim: Corollary 4: CKA drops even when the translation keeps the same separating hyperplane and margins.
key_results.quote: translating one of the subsets in a direction that preserves the linear separability of the representations and the size of the margins while simultaneously decreasing the CKA

key_results.claim: Empirically (synthetic), both linear and RBF CKA collapse under subset translation.
key_results.quote: Despite these multiple notions of “similarity” between X and Y being preserved, the CKA values quickly drop below 0.2 for both linear and RBF CKA.

key_results.claim: Empirically (CIFAR10 CNN last layer), CKA collapses although a linear classifier still separates both sets.
key_results.quote: The CKA values quickly drop to 0, despite the existence of a linear classifier that can classify both sets of representations into the correct classes with > 90% accuracy.

key_results.claim: High early-layer CKA does not mean similar or useful features.
key_results.quote: considerably high CKA similarity values for early layers, does not necessarily translate to more useful, or similar, captured features.

key_results.claim: Whole CKA maps can be set by optimisation with little accuracy change.
key_results.quote: In cases (1) and (2), the network performance is barely hindered by the manipulations of its CKA map.

key_results.claim: The wide-network block structure can be removed without changing performance.
key_results.quote: the specific structures associated with wider network can be completely removed and the map can be nearly identical to the thinner model without changing the performance substantially.

key_results.claim: The optimiser rediscovered subset translation on its own: one class's subset was pushed out along a direction.
key_results.quote: We observe that a a single class has a very noticeable set of points that are translated in a particular direction, away from the general set of classes.

key_results.claim: Manipulated networks behave the same out of distribution.
key_results.quote: We observe that overall the average performance of these models on this out-of-distribution data remains effectively unchanged.

key_results.claim: Recommendation: use several measures and interpretable ones such as orthogonal Procrustes.
key_results.quote: Comparison methods that are straightforward to interpret or which are linked to well understood and simple theoretical properties such as solving the orthogonal Procrustes problem

methods.name: Linear and RBF CKA (minibatch, unbiased HSIC) and layer-by-layer CKA maps
methods.what_it_measures: Alignment of the centred Gram matrices of two representation sets on the same inputs; invariant to orthogonal transforms and isotropic scaling.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Descriptive only. Could support H1 (do pushback and tempting-option conditions change the geometry the same way?) but cannot by itself separate transformed (5) from unchanged (orthogonal re-encodings are invisible) or erased (6) from a subset shift (low CKA without information loss).
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: None by itself; must be paired with probes, Procrustes and patching.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Cheap: activations for the same items under two conditions; minibatch estimator keeps memory low.

methods.name: Subset-translation and single-outlier stress tests (Thm 1, Cor 3, Cor 4; Fig 4)
methods.what_it_measures: How much a similarity measure drops when part of the data is shifted along a direction that keeps separability (or when one point is moved).
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: A sanity check for our own pipeline before calling override vs erased vs transformed: inject a known shift on the flipped subset along a direction orthogonal to the correctness probe and confirm which of our measures react.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Synthetic ground truth; can be combined with steering the same direction in the model to see whether behaviour changes (bypass check).

methods.name: SVM-hyperplane-preserving translation (Cor 4; Fig 4b)
methods.what_it_measures: Whether two sets still share the decision geometry (same hyperplanes, margins) when a global similarity score says they differ.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Bypass (2) and override (4): flipped items may differ from resisted ones along a direction orthogonal to the correctness readout; this test separates 'geometry changed in a behaviour-irrelevant direction' from 'correctness information lost'.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Steer or ablate the shift direction and check whether the answer changes.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Cheap: a linear classifier per layer.

methods.name: Adversarial CKA-map optimisation with distillation (Eq. 3, Algorithm 1)
methods.what_it_measures: Whether a similarity measure can be driven to a target by training while outputs are held fixed.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Stage B 'removed vs hidden' and H3: shows a geometry-based monitor can be gamed by optimisation; we could run a small LoRA version to test whether our fate monitor survives a model trained to fool it.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Compare mechanism (patching) before and after the manipulation.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Cheap for CIFAR CNNs (15-30 epochs); for a 9B LLM a LoRA run with a geometry loss term (our estimate, not tested in paper).
methods.code_available: Not stated; pseudo-code for lambda balancing given (Algorithm 1).

methods.name: PCA visualisation of what changed
methods.what_it_measures: Which points or classes carry a similarity change.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Whether a CKA/RSA difference between conditions is driven by a few items (outliers) or by a coherent group shift.

methods.name: Linear probe accuracy alongside CKA
methods.what_it_measures: Usefulness (linear decodability) of features, to check whether high or low CKA tracks it.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Erased (6) vs decodable: CKA alone cannot say whether the correct answer is still decodable.

controls_worth_copying: Synthetic stress tests with known ground truth (subset translation, single outlier, invertible linear map) run on our similarity pipeline before using it on real activations.
Always report a linear-probe (decodability) result next to any CKA/RSA number.
Check function out of distribution after any manipulation (they used CIFAR-10C).
Same vs different seeds and several random instantiations; several RBF bandwidths (and drop bandwidths where the map is uniformly about 1).
PCA of the representations to see what drives a similarity change.
Use several similarity measures, including Procrustes, and tie each to an explicit notion of similarity.

pitfalls.pitfall: CKA is invariant to orthogonal transforms (rotation, reflection, permutation) and isotropic scaling, so a rotated or sign-flipped re-encoding of the whole set is invisible to it.
pitfalls.quote: it is invariant to orthogonal transformations such as permutations, rotations and reflections and to isotropic scaling.

pitfalls.pitfall: Outlier sensitivity: one point among tens of thousands can collapse CKA.
pitfalls.quote: the fact that the position of a single point out of tens of thousands can so drastically influence the CKA value raises doubts about CKA’s reliability

pitfalls.pitfall: Subset translations along behaviour-irrelevant directions collapse CKA; they can occur naturally and go unnoticed.
pitfalls.quote: these transformations can naturally occur in ANNs, as discussed in Sec. 3, and one wouldn’t necessarily know that they have occurred.

pitfalls.pitfall: Insensitive to removing low-variance directions that matter for probing (from Ding et al.).
pitfalls.quote: Ding et al. (2021) demonstrated that CKA lacks sensitivity to the removal of low variance principal components from the analyzed representations even when this removal significantly decreases probing accuracy.

pitfalls.pitfall: High CKA can come from a few dominant data points (block structure, Nguyen et al. 2022).
pitfalls.quote: the previously observed high CKA similarity between representations of later layers in large capacity models (so-called block structure) is actually caused by a few dominant data points

pitfalls.pitfall: Not a metric: no triangle inequality, so downstream comparisons of CKA values are shaky.
pitfalls.quote: Williams et al. (2021) discussed how CKA does not respect the triangle inequality, which makes it problematic to use CKA values as a similarity measure in downstream analysis tasks.

pitfalls.pitfall: RBF CKA with small bandwidth is uninformative.
pitfalls.quote: RBF CKA with σ = 0.2 × median is significantly less informative than RBF CKA with higher values of σ.

pitfalls.pitfall: An information-preserving invertible linear map can drive linear CKA to about 0.
pitfalls.quote: we observe that even for small values of µ and σ, CKA drops to 0

pitfalls.pitfall: Optimisation can set CKA maps to targets while behaviour stays, so CKA can be gamed.
pitfalls.quote: it is possible to achieve a strong CKA similarity between early and later layers of a well-trained network without noticeably changing the model behaviour.
Such measures are trying to condense a large amount of rich geometrical information from many high-dimensional representations into a single scalar

pitfalls.pitfall: Extra caution for models whose training is not controlled (e.g. open pretrained models, which is our case).
pitfalls.quote: especially when the procedure used to produce the model is not known, consistent, or controlled.

pitfalls.pitfall: Reader note, not stated by the paper: Fig 4b text says CKA 'drops to 0' but the whole-class curve plateaus near 0.18; Fig 16 random-init probes at about chance are unexplained; Fig 11 originals already look close to the target.

limitations_quote: Indeed, some of the problematic transformations we identify are not necessarily encountered in many applications.

limitations_extra.quote: It is not our intention to cast doubts over linear CKA as a representation similarity measure in deep learning, or over recent work using this method.
it is outside the scope of our work to theoretically analyze nonlinear kernel CKA

future_work_quote: Significant work is still required to understand these methods in the context of deep learning representation comparison, what notion of similarity each of them concretely measures

bears_on_fates.how: CKA is invariant to orthogonal transforms, so a whole-set rotation or reflection (one kind of re-encoding) gives the same CKA as no change; and a low CKA can arise without any re-encoding. CKA alone cannot diagnose 'transformed'; use Procrustes alignment plus probe transfer across conditions.

Low CKA does not mean the information is gone: a subset translation or one outlier drives CKA toward 0 while a linear classifier still separates classes with > 90% accuracy. Erasure must be shown with decodability (probes) and causal tests, not with CKA.

Our inference, not the paper's: an added competing signal on only the flipped items (e.g. a push along an 'agree with user' direction) is exactly a subset translation, so CKA between neutral and pressured activations would drop even if correctness stays decodable. A CKA drop may signal an added component rather than a loss; test by centring each group (flipped, resisted) separately and recomputing.

The theorem's remark that a shift orthogonal to the next layer's weights has no functional effect is the geometric form of 'present but causally inert'; representational differences need patching before they count as mechanism.
Nothing direct; CKA says nothing about where a readout threshold sits.

bears_on_group_angle: The most directly relevant warning for our RSA/CKA plans. (1) CKA/RSA compress the geometry of a point cloud into one number that a few items or a subset shift can dominate; for H1 (pressure-specific geometry) report bootstrap or leave-one-item-out ranges and check outliers with PCA. (2) CKA cannot see rotations/reflections, so it cannot carry the transformed-vs-erased call; pair it with orthogonal Procrustes (with and without a translation term), principal angles between class-mean subspaces, and probe transfer from neutral to pressured activations. (3) Flipped-vs-resisted point clouds may differ mainly by a mean shift of one group; principal angles on centred data would ignore that shift, while CKA would over-react to it, so track the mean-shift vector and the subspace separately. (4) Because CKA can be optimised to arbitrary values with behaviour fixed, a geometry measure is not safe as a Stage B pass/fail monitor. The paper itself recommends multiple measures, Procrustes and visualisation.
architecture_location: No LLM or component-level claims. In CNN/ResNet/VGG/ViT layer maps it shows that 'where' conclusions drawn from CKA maps (early-vs-late similarity, wide-network block structure) can be created or erased without behaviour change, so a claim like 'pressure and neutral representations diverge at layer L' needs more than a CKA map. It also shows early layers score high CKA between networks with unrelated features (about 0.5-1.0 at layers 1-2, approx from Figs 2 and 15).
actionable_fix: No model fix. It gives a monitor-design rule: do not use CKA (or any single-scalar similarity) as the test of whether a fix removed or merely hid a failure, since training can move CKA maps to targets with at most 0.5 accuracy points change in the linear-CKA CNN cases (85.9% to 85.4-85.5%; up to 1.6 points for RBF sigma 0.8, 85.9% to 84.3%). Use causal checks (patching), decodability (probes) and behaviour, and if a geometry monitor is kept, combine several measures and stress-test it with subset translations and outliers.
reuse_verdict: adapt - copy the stress tests (subset translation, single outlier, invertible map) and the advice to pair CKA with Procrustes, probes and PCA; keep linear CKA only as a descriptive companion; avoid using CKA alone to call transformed vs erased, or as a Stage B monitor.
relevance_to_project: Relevant as a methods warning for the group angle, not as evidence about LLMs: every experiment is a small vision model on CIFAR10 (2022), with no language models, facts or social pressure. Its subset-translation theorem maps closely onto our setting, where only the flipped items might be shifted along an 'agree with user' direction; that would crash CKA while the correct answer stays decodable. It should change how we use CKA/RSA for H1 and for transformed-vs-erased, and it argues for Procrustes plus probe transfer as the primary tools.
